🤖 THREEHALVES — THE CENTAUR ROBOT Threehalves is a 7-foot-tall teleoperated robot developed by Satyress. Its design combines a human-like torso and arms with a powerful four-legged chassis, creating a mechanical centaur built for environments that are too dangerous for humans. The idea behind Threehalves is simple: instead of sending a person into extreme heat, unstable terrain, darkness, hazardous industrial environments or disaster zones, a skilled operator can control the robot remotely and perform the work from a safer location. Unlike many humanoid robots, Threehalves is designed around tools and equipment that humans already use. Its modular limbs and quick-connect system allow it to be adapted for different tasks, while its four-legged platform provides stability on difficult terrain. The most unsettling part is probably its appearance. With its enormous size, humanoid body, four mechanical legs and distinctive horned head, Threehalves looks less like a traditional industrial machine and more like something from a science-fiction horror movie. But behind the terrifying design is a serious engineering concept: putting the machine in danger instead of the human. Threehalves is still a developing robotics project, but it represents a strange glimpse into a future where dangerous jobs could be performed remotely — with a human controlling the machine from a distance. And honestly… it might be one of the creepiest robots ever built. 👁️ #threehalves #robot #baal #satyress #horrortok

Do you want this guy rolling around your home? Maybe if it does laundry… Weave Robotics, a San Francisco startup backed by Y Combinator, has launched Isaac 1, a home robot designed to tackle laundry and light tidying. Rather than following the humanoid trend, Isaac 1 uses a wheeled base and extends from three feet to five foot nine depending on the task, with two articulated arms offering an 80-inch vertical reach.  It's built to autonomously locate dirty clothes, manage hampers, and fold garments, though human teleoperators can step in remotely when it gets stuck. And yes, that means someone may occasionally see inside your home through its cameras.  Priced at $7,999 upfront or $449 a month, it undercuts 1X's Neo by more than half. California deliveries begin this fall. #fyp #robot #techtok

En un mundo donde la tecnología avanza a pasos agigantados, observamos cómo los robots comienzan a asumir tareas que antes parecían imposibles. En este video, un robot masilla las juntas de los paneles de yeso, demostrando precisión y eficiencia en cada movimiento, sea real o animado, nos invita a reflexionar:  En el futuro, los robots realizarán muchos de los trabajos difíciles, repetitivos y peligrosos que hoy enfrentamos. Pero hay algo que las máquinas no pueden replicar: nuestra creatividad, nuestra ética y nuestra capacidad de soñar.Los robots serán nuestros aliados, facilitando nuestras labores y permitiéndonos enfocarnos en lo que realmente importa. Seremos nosotros quienes diseñemos, innovemos y tomemos decisiones basadas en valores humanos.Mientras los robots se encargan del trabajo arduo, nosotros, los humanos, seguiremos liderando con imaginación y corazón. Porque aunque la tecnología avance, la chispa de la humanidad nunca será reemplazada.  ¿Qué opinas sobre el futuro de la tecnología en la construcción?
